chunks: 11 - My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. 'Abdullah and 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. They said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. 'Isa narrated to us from Muhammad b. Khalid al-Barqi from Ahmad b. Yazid al-Nishapuri. He said: 'Umar b. Ibrahim al-Hashimi narrated to me from 'Abd al-Malik b. 'Umayr from Usayd b. Safwan, the companion of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He said:

When it was the day that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) passed away, the place was jolted with weeping, and the people were stunned just like the day the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) passed away. A weeping man came hurrying, saying 'inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' [to Allah we belong and to Him we return], and he was saying: 'Today, the vicegerency of prophethood has been cut off.' Then he stood at the door of the house that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was in, and he said:

May Allah have mercy on you, O Abu al-Hasan. You were the first of the people to enter Islam, the sincerest of them in faith, the most intense of them in certainty, the most God-fearing of them before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, the greatest of them in effort, the most prudent of them over the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the most protective over his companions, the best of them in virtues, the most honoured of them in precedent, the highest of them in rank, the nearest of them to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), the most similar to him in guidance, character, demeanor, and action, the most noble of them in status, and the most honoured to him. So may Allah reward you with goodness on behalf of Islam, His Messenger, and the Muslims. You were strengthened when his companions became weak, you emerged when they settled down, you rose when they languished, and you adhered to the path of His Messenger when they were his companions. You were truly his vicegerent—you did not quarrel nor plead despite the hypocrites, the anger of disbelievers, the hatred of enviers, and the malice of transgressors. You established the matter when they failed, you spoke when they stuttered, and you proceeded with the light of Allah when they halted—so they followed you and were guided.

You were the quietest of them in voice, the highest in surpassing, the least of them in speech, the most correct in eloquence, the greatest in opinion, the bravest in heart, the most intense in certainty, the best in action, and the most knowledgeable in matters. You were, by Allah, a leader of the religion—first when the people dispersed, and last when they failed. For the believers, you were a merciful father when they became your dependents. You carried the burdens they were too weak for, preserved what they wasted, were mindful of what they neglected. You strove when they gathered, rose when they panicked, were patient when they hurried, comprehended what they fell behind in, and they attained through you what they did not expect. For the disbelievers, you were an outpouring punishment; for the believers, rain and abundance. By Allah, you soared with its blessings, succeeded with its gifts, secured its precedents, and went with its virtues. Your argument never failed, your heart never deviated, your insight never weakened, you were never cowardly nor treacherous. You were like a mountain that storms cannot shake and catastrophes cannot remove. And you were as the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: weak in your body, strong in the command of Allah, humble in yourself, great with Allah the Mighty and Majestic, grand in the earth, majestic with the believers. No one could find fault in you, no speaker could find defect in you, no one could covet you, and no one received leniency from you. The weak and humiliated before you are strong and mighty until they are given their rights; and the strong and mighty before you are weak and humiliated until rights are taken from them. The near and the far are equal before you in that. Your way is truth, honesty, and gentleness. Your word is judgment and decisive. Your affair is forbearance and resolve. Your opinion is knowledge and determination. You departed after the path had been made clear, hardships eased, fires extinguished. Through you the religion was balanced, through you Islam and the believers were strengthened. You preceded by far, and you exhausted those after you greatly. You became too great for tears. Your tragedy is great in the heavens, and your calamity has devastated the people. So: to Allah we belong, and to Him we shall return. We are pleased with Allah's decree, and we submit to His command. By Allah, the Muslims shall never be afflicted with something like this again. For the believers, you were a fortified cave; and upon the disbelievers, harshness and rage. May Allah reunite you with His Prophet, and not deprive us of your reward, and not misguide us after you.

The people were silent until he completed his speech. He wept and made the companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) weep. Then they sought after him, but they did not find him.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful — the title given to Imam Ali (as)
key_terms.إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون: To Allah we belong and to Him we return — Quranic phrase (2:156) recited upon affliction
key_terms.خلافة النبوة: Vicegerency of prophethood — succession to the Prophet's authority
key_terms.كهف حصين: Fortified cave — metaphor for a place of safety and refuge
key_terms.يعسوب: Ya'sub (leader/chief) — a title the Prophet gave to Ali, meaning 'leader of the believers'

ai.seo_question: What eulogy was delivered at the funeral of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) and what virtues did it praise?
ai.summary: This hadith records a famous eulogy delivered by an unidentified man at the funeral of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), Commander of the Faithful. The speaker enumerates Ali's supreme virtues—his primacy in Islam, sincerity of faith, closeness to the Prophet, and unmatched leadership qualities. He praises Ali's steadfastness when others faltered, his justice that treated strong and weak equally, and his unwavering commitment to truth. The eulogy concludes with the Quranic phrase of grief (2:156) and a prayer that Allah reunite Ali with the Prophet. The mysterious speaker disappeared after his speech, leading to speculation that he was al-Khidr or an angel.
